questions.question: A 23-year-old man from Somalia presents to your clinic.

parts.text: Give four tests and the infectious diseases they screen for that are indicated in this man.

parts_raw.text: Give four tests and the infectious diseases they screen for that are indicated in this man.

questions.model_answer: (1) HIV serology (ELISA/4th-generation antigen-antibody) - HIV. (2) Interferon-gamma release assay or tuberculin skin test, with chest radiograph - latent/active tuberculosis. (3) Schistosoma serology - schistosomiasis. (4) Strongyloides serology - strongyloidiasis.
questions.beyond_mandell: Canadian refugee screening guidelines (Pottie et al., CMAJ 2011) additionally recommend HBV, HCV and syphilis serology in newly arrived refugees.

cohort_answer.text: HIV, Hep Bs Ag and Ab, Hep C ab, syphilis – serology + VDRL, strongyloides serology, schistosomiasis serology, tuberculosis – CXR/ TST

questions.question: A 23-year-old man from Sudan is a refugee in your clinic.
questions.question_raw: 4. 23 year old man from Sudan is a refugee in your clinic.

parts.text: Name two screening tests for infectious diseases that are indicated.
Name six infectious diseases, which may be asymptomatic, that you could screen this person for.

parts_raw.text: Name two screening tests for infectious diseases are indicated? (2)
Name 6 infectious diseases, that may be asymptomatic, that you could screen this person for. (3)

questions.model_answer: a) (1) HIV serology. (2) Interferon-gamma release assay or tuberculin skin test (with chest radiograph) for tuberculosis. b) (1) HIV. (2) Tuberculosis (latent). (3) Schistosomiasis. (4) Strongyloidiasis. (5) Syphilis. (6) Chronic hepatitis B (or hepatitis C).
questions.beyond_mandell: Hepatitis B and C are drawn from Canadian refugee screening guidelines (Pottie et al., CMAJ 2011) rather than this chapter, which frames asymptomatic screening around HIV/STI, TB, schistosomiasis and strongyloidiasis.

cohort_answer.text: Screening tests: HIV and Strongyloides serology, LTBI (CXR or IGRA), Syphilis serology. Diseases to screen for: HIV, Strongyloides, Schistosoma, Hep C and Hep B, LTBI, Syphilis (also urine chlam/gono in adults)

questions.model_answer: (1) HIV serology - HIV. (2) Interferon-gamma release assay or tuberculin skin test, with chest radiograph - latent/active tuberculosis. (3) Schistosoma serology - schistosomiasis. (4) Strongyloides serology - strongyloidiasis.

cohort_answer.text: HIV Serology (ELISA) - HIV; STI screen: Syphilis Serology, NAT for GC, CT; CXR - TB + TST or IGRA if available; HBV Serology - HBV (where prevalence is >2%); Hep C; Malaria - not on initial screening recommendations on app by steve; Strongyloides, schistosoma serology; Varicella IgG immune status if >13 y.o only

questions.question: Name three tests that Immigration Canada performs on incoming immigrants and refugees.

parts.text: Name three tests that Immigration Canada does on incoming immigrants/refugees.

parts_raw.text: Name 3 tests that Immigration Canada does on incoming immigrants/refugees?

questions.model_answer: (1) Chest radiograph (postero-anterior) for tuberculosis (applicants aged 11 and older). (2) Syphilis serology (aged 15 and older). (3) HIV serology (aged 15 and older). [Urinalysis, aged 5 and older, is also part of the immigration medical examination.]
questions.beyond_mandell: Based on the IRCC Immigration Medical Examination requirements, not covered in this Mandell chapter.

cohort_answer.text: Urinalysis (>=5 years); Chest x-ray (postero-anterior view) (>=11 years); Syphilis (>=15 years); HIV (>=15 years).
